title: Extraction of brain tissue with fluorogold-labelled neurons for electron microscopy imaging
author: Enrico Zampese
materials: Optional: repeat saline injection to prevent dehydration
Under the hood, pour PBS and fixative solutionsin 50ml tubes.
Start running PBS through the tubing.
Terminally anesthetize the mouse according to institutional protocols.
Decapitate the mouse with the scissor.
Leave the brain in fixative overnight at 4C.
Isolation of region containing Fluorogold-labelled cell
The transmission electron microscope is operated at 80kHz
Different levels of magnification can be adopted.

steps.title: Prepare fluorogold solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve fluorogold powder in sterile 0.9 % NaCl saline to obtain a 1 % (w/v) working solution.

steps.title: Prepare post‑operative cages
steps.instruction: Set up a clean empty mouse cage on a heating pad and a second cage with gel food for post‑operative care.

steps.title: Set up sterile workspace
steps.instruction: Arrange a sterile working area and assemble the stereotaxic frame.

steps.title: Weigh the mouse
steps.instruction: Measure the mouse’s weight and record it for dosage calculations.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in an induction chamber delivering 2.5 % isoflurane at 200 ml/min flow rate.

steps.title: Clip hair and position mouse
steps.instruction: Quickly clip hair over the surgical area, transfer the mouse onto the stereotaxic frame placed on a heating pad with a temperature probe, secure the mouth on the nose cone, and restart anesthesia directed to the nose cone.

substeps.instruction: Allow ~5 min for deep anesthesia before stopping the induction flow.
Adjust the heating pad so the probe reads 33‑37 °C.

steps.title: Apply eye ointment and analgesia
steps.instruction: Apply ophthalmic ointment to the eyes and inject the analgesic volume calculated from the mouse weight (plus optional saline to prevent dehydration).

steps.title: Secure ear‑bars and verify head
steps.instruction: Insert and tighten the ear‑bars; after exposing the skull, ensure the head is not visibly tilted.

steps.title: Disinfect surgical site
steps.instruction: Clean the incision area with a povidone‑iodine swab followed by an ethanol swab and repeat the sequence three times.

steps.title: Apply local anesthetic
steps.instruction: Apply 0.15 % bupivacaine (line‑block) under the skull skin before proceeding (instead of EMLA cream at the end).

steps.title: Make scalp incision
steps.instruction: Using fine scissors, make an anterior‑posterior incision to expose the skull.

steps.title: Mark bregma and zero coordinates
steps.instruction: Insert a glass pipette (optionally pre‑marked with non‑toxic food dye) onto the stereotaxic arm, gently touch the bregma intersection, and set the coordinate reader to zero.

steps.title: Locate lambda and adjust head
steps.instruction: Move the pipette to lambda (lambdoid‑sagittal intersection), record its position relative to bregma, and adjust the head until dorso‑ventral (D/V) and medio‑lateral (M/L) deviations are minimized.

substeps.instruction: Zero the coordinates at bregma again and repeat bregma/lambda measurements until satisfactory.

steps.title: Calculate coordinate adjustment
steps.instruction: Measure the B‑L distance, divide by the reference distance 4.21 to obtain an adjustment ratio; for adult mice the ratio ≈1 (no adjustment), for smaller mice multiply reference coordinates by the ratio to obtain final coordinates.

steps.title: Mark injection sites
steps.instruction: Move the pipette to the adjusted A/P and M/L coordinates, mark the spot, and repeat on the opposite side for bilateral injections, ensuring minimal D/V deviation between sides.

steps.title: Drill skull holes
steps.instruction: Remove the marker pipette and drill a hole at each marked position; clean blood and debris with sterile saline and sterile cotton swabs.

steps.title: Load fluorogold into micropipette
steps.instruction: Insert a micropipette with volumetric references into the holder, connect it to a syringe, draw up the desired volume of fluorogold solution by negative pressure.

steps.title: Insert pipette to dura
steps.instruction: Lower the fluorogold‑filled pipette into the drilled hole until the tip contacts the dura and zero the D/V coordinate.

steps.title: Inject fluorogold into brain
steps.instruction: Gradually lower the pipette tip to the target D/V coordinate and inject the fluorogold at ~150 nl/min by gentle positive pressure.

substeps.instruction: Release pressure and leave the pipette in place for 5‑10 min to allow diffusion.

steps.title: Recover mouse post‑injection
steps.instruction: Remove the mouse from the stereotaxic frame, place it in the clean empty heated cage until deambulatory (≈10‑15 min), then transfer to the gel‑food cage on the heating pad.

steps.title: Post‑operative care
steps.instruction: At 24 h administer a second dose of Metacam and apply antibiotic ointment to the sutured skin; monitor health daily and give additional Metacam or saline if needed; keep the mouse on a heating pad for at least 4 days before moving to standard housing.

steps.title: Schedule sacrifice
steps.instruction: Sacrifice the mouse 5‑6 days after fluorogold injection for tissue extraction.

steps.title: Set up perfusion system
steps.instruction: Attach the perfusion needle to the connector at the tubing end; optionally use a switchable connector system pre‑loaded with PBS and fixative and a vacuum‑trap for waste collection.

steps.title: Verify deep anesthesia
steps.instruction: Bring the anesthetized mouse to a dissection tray and confirm lack of pain reflex by pinching a posterior paw.

steps.title: Position mouse for perfusion
steps.instruction: Secure the mouse supine on the tray, head oriented away from the operator, tray slightly inclined with head pointing slightly downward.

steps.title: Expose thoracic cavity
steps.instruction: Hold skin below the sternum with tweezers, cut the skin to expose the peritoneal cavity and rib cage (diaphragm intact); cut fascia toward the head; then cut the diaphragm without damaging the beating heart, cut and lift the rib cage, optionally hold with a needle; liver should become visible.

steps.title: Perfuse with PBS then fixative
steps.instruction: Insert the needle (connected to a peristaltic pump circulating PBS) into the left ventricle, pinch the right atrium with spring scissors, allow dark‑red blood to flow, wash blood while the heart beats; when the liver appears blood‑free, switch perfusion to fixative.

substeps.instruction: Rinse briefly with water while maintaining needle position.

steps.title: Fixative volume based on weight
steps.instruction: Perfuse each mouse with a fixative volume approximately equal to its weight in grams (e.g., 20 ml fixative for a 20 g mouse).

substeps.instruction: Observe tissue contraction as an indicator of successful fixation.

steps.title: Terminate perfusion and collect carcass
steps.instruction: After the calculated fixative volume has passed, stop perfusion, remove the needle, and note that the carcass is very stiff.

steps.title: Dissect brain
steps.instruction: Using fine scissors, cut the skin, expose the median skull line, remove the posterior skull, make two diagonal cuts past bregma toward the eyes and two cuts along the lambdoidal sutures; open the skull with tweezers, gently lift the brain with a spatula and place it into the remaining fixative in a Falcon tube.

substeps.instruction: Close the tube and gently shake.
Dispose of the carcass in a carcass bag.

steps.title: Dispose of waste
steps.instruction: Discard all fixative waste (liquid and solid) and sharps according to institutional guidelines.

steps.title: Rinse brain before slicing
steps.instruction: Remove the brain from overnight fixative, rinse three times for 10 min each with PBS, and keep the brain in a clean tube with fresh PBS.

steps.title: Prepare agarose support
steps.instruction: Cut a 0.5 × 0.5 in rectangle of agarose for later use.

steps.title: Set vibratome parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the vibratome to 400 µm slice thickness, 1 mm oscillation amplitude, and a speed of ~0.2‑0.3 mm/s.

steps.title: Trim brain for gluing
steps.instruction: Remove the brain from PBS onto a weighing bowl, cut off the rostral portion to create a flat surface for gluing, and remove the cerebellum.

steps.title: Glue brain to slicing stage
steps.instruction: Apply super glue to the slicing chamber stage, gently attach the brain (ventral side facing the blade, rostral side at the bottom); optionally glue the agarose piece on the side not facing the blade.

steps.title: Mount stage and fill chamber
steps.instruction: Place the stage in the vibratome tray, attach to the vibratome, and fill the cutting chamber with PBS.

steps.title: Cut brain slices
steps.instruction: Lower the blade holder into the chamber, adjust settings, and when near the region of interest cut 400‑500 µm slices; collect each slice with a transfer pipette or tweezers into separate wells of a collection plate, recording the order.

substeps.instruction: If desired, move the blade closer before cutting to avoid unnecessary thin slices.

steps.title: Finish slicing and clean
steps.instruction: Stop the vibratome, return the blade holder to a safe position, discard extra solution and remaining tissue, dispose of all waste and sharps per guidelines, and wash the apparatus and tools.

steps.title: Microscope observation of slices
steps.instruction: Transfer the plate to the microscope station, turn on the microscope, and view slices with a fluorogold‑compatible filter set.

steps.title: Select best fluorogold slice
steps.instruction: Identify the slice with the strongest fluorogold signal, sketch its exact anatomical location for later reference.

steps.title: Dissect tissue block
steps.instruction: Move the selected slice to a PBS‑filled petri dish, dissect a 1 mm × 1 mm square containing the region of interest, and sketch the fluorogold distribution within the block.

steps.title: Transfer block to fixative
steps.instruction: Under a chemical hood, place the tissue block into a hinged plastic vial containing fixative solution and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Send to EM core
steps.instruction: Provide the fixative‑containing vial and anatomical sketches to the Northwestern University Center for Advanced Microscopy (NU CAM) for further processing.

steps.title: EM core processing (summary)
steps.instruction: Core will post‑fix in buffered 2 % OsO₄, stain in 3 % uranyl acetate, dehydrate through ascending ethanol, transition to propylene oxide, embed in Embed 812, section with an ultramicrotome (Leica Ultracut UC6), collect 1 µm Toluidine Blue O sections and 70 nm sections on 200 mesh copper grids, and stain the latter with uranyl acetate and Reynolds lead citrate.

steps.title: TEM imaging preparation
steps.instruction: Ensure prior training and approval; turn on the transmission electron microscope, use liquid nitrogen as cooling agent (handle with cryo‑gloves).

steps.title: Acquire TEM images
steps.instruction: Insert one sample grid according to instructions, locate cell bodies at low magnification, identify retrogradely‑labelled cells by electron‑dense vesicular or multilamellar structures, then collect high‑resolution images; collect residual liquid nitrogen and remove the grid per instructions.
